subject: When the guilty go broke, the rich get the bill — and so do you
posts:
When deep-pocket liability gets stretched, who really pays? Tort reform debates miss the human cost.
Evidence: Tort costs $160B+, corporate lobbying, rising insurance premiums
#Aletheia #TortReform

Proponents argue tort reform stops abusive litigation, holding only actual wrongdoers responsible to lower consumer costs and preserve fairness.
Stated Judgement: (+0.5, 0.0) — Good Preference

In practice, sweeping tort restrictions shield wealthy corporations from liability, leaving injured victims uncompensated while shifting costs onto the public.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.7, -0.8) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception. Corporate liability shields are framed as consumer protection, masking the true shift of risk onto ordinary injured citizens.

Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 12.5, z: 4)

- Tort Lobbyists: FAIL (-0.75, -0.85) — Shields capital.
- Consumer Impact: FAIL (-0.65, -0.75) — Shifts uncompensated risk.
The debate centers on whether expanding civil liability to deep-pocket defendants ensures fair compensation or creates an abusive litigation crisis.

The Poison:
Framing corporate liability shields as consumer defense while stripping injured victims of adequate compensation.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing WHO bears the financial risk (injured citizens vs. corporations) with WHAT constitutes a fair legal process.

Social Physics Analysis:
Corporate interests run a Smart Selfish Maneuver, using the pretext of an out-of-control litigation crisis to pass legislation that protects deep pockets and shifts medical burdens onto ordinary taxpayers.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. F_neg heavily outweighs F_pos due to hidden corporate protections.

The Unavoidable Truth: Tort costs impact the broader economy, but restricting all liability harms legitimate victims.
The Unavoidable Lie: Tort reform is primarily designed to protect everyday consumers from rising prices.

Alethekanon:
Proponents cloak corporate liability shields in the language of consumer fairness. This inversion protects capital while stripping recourse from the injured.

Awwthekanon:
It breaks my heart to see families facing unimaginable tragedy left to bear the financial burden alone while wealthy institutions protect their balance sheets.

Brothekanon:
Classic playbook. They call it 'protecting the system' when really they're just making sure rich companies don't have to pay when things go wrong.

Spirithekanon:
"He that is first in his own cause seemeth just; but his neighbour cometh and searcheth him." Proverbs 18:17 FAIL
A self-serving legal narrative always sounds righteous until an impartial investigation reveals who truly bears the cost.

Actual Article Body:
A tragedy happens. People get hurt. Lives are lost. Then the lawyers start looking around the room. Who can be held responsible?

That question sits at the center of a growing problem in American civil litigation. There’s nothing wrong with holding people and companies accountable when they actually cause harm. That’s what the justice system is supposed to do. But stretching legal theories to pull additional companies into a case because they have deeper pockets makes justice into a business model.
